datasetName: NASA OSDR RadLab ISS Radiation Dosimetry Telemetry
researchObjective: Quantify spatial and temporal radiation dose rates and dose equivalent rates across ISS modules (US Lab, Columbus) to track Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR) and South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) passes.
studySubjects: DOSTEL active silicon detectors (DOSTEL-1, DOSTEL-2) mounted inside ISS pressurized modules
timeCoverage: Multi-year continuous telemetry (51.6° inclination LEO, 400 km altitude)
accessRestrictions: Public Open Access (NASA Open Data Policy / CCO 1.0)
relevanceToMedula: Directly maps to MEDULA radiation records schema (ambient_radiation_rate in µSv/h and cumulative_dose in mSv). Used to validate radiation hazard monitoring without biological fabrication.
provenance: NASA OSDR RadLab API telemetry payload verified against published ISS DOSTEL calibration reference standards.

datasetName: NASA OSDR Environmental Data App: ISS Cabin Atmosphere Telemetry
researchObjective: Continuous monitoring of pressurized cabin atmospheric parameters (CO2, temperature, relative humidity, pressure) across ISS mission increments to evaluate environmental habitability and biological payload conditions.
studySubjects: ISS Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) sensors across US Orbital Segment modules
accessRestrictions: Public Open Access (NASA Open Science Data Repository)
relevanceToMedula: Directly maps to MEDULA Module 04 environmentalRecords store. Provides verified cabin parameters to contextualize astronaut health patterns without asserting causation.
provenance: NASA OSDR Environmental Data App verified orbital telemetry payload.

datasetName: Effects of 60-day Head-Down Tilt Bed Rest on Human Skeletal Muscle (WISE-2005)
researchObjective: Investigate microgravity-induced physiological deconditioning in humans using a 60-day 6° head-down tilt (HDT) bed rest ground analog, measuring muscle disuse atrophy, heart rate recovery, and resistive exercise countermeasures.
studySubjects: 24 healthy adult female human volunteers (Women's International Space Simulation for Exploration)
timeCoverage: 60-day head-down tilt bed rest campaign with pre- and post-ambulatory phases
accessRestrictions: Public Open Access for normalized study tables and metadata; raw identifiable human medical charts restricted under NASA/ESA IRB governance.
sourceSystem: NASA OSDR Biological Data Repository (GeneLab & ALSDA)
relevanceToMedula: Validates human physiological response to simulated microgravity disuse; provides empirical evidence for MEDULA's physical performance baseline decay models.
provenance: NASA OSDR Biological Data API dataset OSD-51 (GLDS-51 / LSDS-41).

datasetName: Stem Cell Differentiation Toward Osteoblast Onboard the ISS
researchObjective: Evaluate human mesenchymal stem cell differentiation into osteoblasts in orbital microgravity to identify molecular pathways contributing to spaceflight bone mineral density reduction.
studySubjects: Human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells cultured in microgravity vs terrestrial 1g ground controls
relevanceToMedula: Supplies foundational space biology evidence for Hazard 4 (Gravity Fields) bone homeostasis disruption.
provenance: NASA OSDR Biological Data API dataset OSD-546.

datasetName: NASA Spaceflight Standard Measures Cohort Norms & Protocol Repository
researchObjective: Establish longitudinal, standardized physiological, behavioral, and biological reference trajectories across astronaut cohorts flying on long-duration ISS expedition increments.
accessRestrictions: RESTRICTED — NASA Institutional Review Board (IRB) & Lifetime Surveillance of Astronaut Health (LSAH). Raw individual astronaut records contain Protected Health Information (PHI) and cannot be publicly downloaded without formal NASA Data Request Protocol approval.
sourceSystem: NASA Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA) / Human Research Program
relevanceToMedula: Serves as the scientific foundation for MEDULA's metric taxonomy, unit standards, and baseline computation windows. Cohort reference medians inform baseline validation rules without exposing individual astronaut records.
provenance: NASA Spaceflight Standard Measures Project Manual & Published HRP Cohort Summary Norms.
